correction: Diagram layout repair only: two separated panels with readable period, slope, piece and boundary labels; exact cable and trefoil peripheral data retained.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Lift of P_{2,1} to the universal cover of its parallel torus
diagram_math_checks.check: The drawing displacement is (6,2); with 3 drawing units per longitude and 2 per meridian this is the same coordinate displacement (2,1). Both longitude periods are shown, separated by the dashed midpoint. The arrow has positive longitudinal and meridional direction, and its endpoints project to the same torus point.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The Example parameterization has arguments (4πs,2πs), and Proof 1.1 gives orbit slope 2λ_V+μ_V. No crossing or planar knot projection is asserted.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Trefoil exterior E_K and cable space X_{P_{2,1}} meeting at T_c
diagram_math_checks.check: The common edge remains T_c. The exterior satellite boundary is labeled on the cable-space side; E_K is the outside component. The shared edge does not represent the satellite boundary.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The local satellite-pattern definition gives T_c=e(∂V), X_P=V\int N(P), and satellite boundary e(∂N(P)); Proof 5.1 identifies the outside component with E_K.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Regular-fiber slopes on the common torus
diagram_math_checks.check: The labels remain f_K=λ+6μ and f_P=2λ+μ. In the ordered basis (μ,λ), their columns (1,2) and (6,1) have determinant −11, so the figure preserves the nonparallel slopes.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Read the actual torus-knot supplier Statement and Proof 4.2–5.1: λ=hμ^(−pq), hence h=λ+6μ for the trefoil. Read the satellite-pattern and meridian/longitude definitions: the companion embedding matches the positive meridian and preferred longitude. Assigned Proof 1.1 and 2.1 establish the cable slope and determinant.
